title: A check that each open PR is assigned to one session only
why: Coordinator's 16:49 CST record via the retrospective session (reversible pick): #1166 and #2366 went to two sessions.
note: triage's merge-main builder worked both at 16:10-16:59 CST. Express lane started 12:43 CST Nov 13 (coordinator 12:44 CST): session_013NEJL27Zw8otLsDBqaNN61, with step release-check-vs-batch-head. Coordinator 18:55 CST Nov 13 (18:54): member #3231 (lane session_013NEJL27Zw8otLsDBqaNN61, in combine-g3) adds a check that fails any PR whose commits name more than one session; combine-g1's lane lint on #3313 (head 25d4be445) FAILed on it. Coordinator's undoable pick: g1 rebuilds without #3231 as combine-g1b. #3231 needs a ruling before it merges alone: page item 788 (b own lane commits only, recommended; a exempt combined PRs; c drop the check). Owner 19:23 CST Nov 13 on item 788: "none of these", "this check as it is isnt built right imo". #3231 stays held; the owner is asked on the item which part (what it counts, or that it fails multi-session PRs) is wrong. Item stays open. Owner 19:59 CST Nov 13 on item 788: "this check as it is isnt built right"; then "just pick a recommended easy option for now and we review again later". Triage took b (the check reads only the PR's own lane commits) as an interim (ruling own-788-b-interim-review-later). Lane session_013NEJL27Zw8otLsDBqaNN61 told. Undo: the owner repicks at review. #3231 stays held until rebuilt to b and reviewed. Lane 20:02 CST Nov 13 (20:00): rebuild to option b started. Its interim definition of "own commits": the first-parent commits of base..head, so a combined PR's member commits (second parents of the combiner's merge commits) do not count; a normal lane keeps all its commits, so the original incident (a second session's commit on top) still fails. Named limit: a lane that merges another open PR's head also drops that head's commits. No exemption form. Reversible; the owner may want another definition at his review. Lane measure 20:16 CST Nov 13 (20:15; its read, unchecked by triage): on #3314 (head ad8c791056b7, base 309fa5ed5b) git log --first-parent is 41 commits and exactly 1 carries a Claude-Session trailer (g1's records reset); merge commits carry none; trailerless commits count as no session. So the first-parent rule reads one session and #3314 passes; the old all-commits rule reads 36 sessions and would refuse it. One non-merge first-parent commit by the combiner is the combiner's own session, not a second path. The rule fails a combined PR only if two sessions each put a trailered commit on its first-parent path (the incident shape). No new named limit beyond the two filed (trailerless uncounted; a lane that merges another open head drops that head's commits). Members are second parents under git merge --no-ff (SKILL.md line 65), so they drop out. Builder still running; this goes in the PR description.
